=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:28336-28363 (the `0:ok)` arm of the new case statement) | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The empty check-run page (`PR_CHECKS_LAST_TOTAL=0 → D_check`) fires before the unreadable CI runs warn (`PR_CHECKS_RUNS_READ=false`).
  WHY: When the Actions runs listing is unreadable on a head with no check-runs, the sweep pages D_check and continues before reaching the warn-without-page path; the cited test only covers a positive `wait_total`.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Require the qualifying `[ai-autofix]` / `[judge-fix]` commits to be authored or committed by that same identity." (Issue #7313 recommendation under the `noop-force-merge-forged-comment-gates` finding, plus the same wording echoed in the agents.md fragment describing the Gate C identity check.)
  Expected change site: Gate C (the `N_LATEST_PROD_TS` jq filter) in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` around lines 28043-28054, and the helper `NOOP_PRODUCTIVE_COMMIT_NAME` / `NOOP_PRODUCTIVE_COMMIT_EMAIL` declarations around lines 27884-27892.
  Evidence of absence: Gate C's jq filter checks only `commit.author.name`/`commit.author.email` and `commit.committer.name`/`commit.committer.email` against the fixed `codex-bot`/`codex@users.noreply.github.com` pair. It never inspects the commit's GitHub-verified `author.login` / `committer.login` against `N_TRUSTED_LOGIN` (or another trusted identity like the GH_PAT login). A same-repo PR author with write access can set `git config user.name "codex-bot"` and `git config user.email "codex@users.noreply.github.com"` before pushing a commit; the commit message prefix `[ai-autofix]` and the forged git identity then pass Gate C while the real GitHub actor remains an arbitrary user. The in-line comment at lines 27887-27892 explicitly states that the constant pair is the GH_PAT login's identity — but only the git author/committer fields are checked, not the GitHub login that GitHub binds to a real account. The GitHub `pulls/<n>/commits` payload already exposes `author.login` and `committer.login`; the filter has them available and ignores them. The last run did not change this; the gap remains unaddressed.
  severity=BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
